newsitem.title: KENYA: ATHLETICS-KIPTANUI CLEARED TO RUN AT KENYAN TRIALS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-KIPTANUI CLEARED TO RUN AT KENYAN TRIALS.

text.p: Steeplechase world record holder Moses Kiptanui was cleared to run in the Kenyan trials for the world athletics championships on Thursday and took a confident step towards the Athens event.
Kiptanui's employers, the Armed Forces, had earlier pleaded with athletics chiefs to bar the three-times world champion after he did not compete at the Forces championships earlier this month.
But the Forces changed their mind and Kiptanui took fourth place in his heat behind winner Joseph Koskei to move into the second round of the 3,000 metres steeplechase.

"We barred him on the strength of that letter from his employers. However, when his employers rescinded the decision, we reinstated him," said David Okeyo, secretary general of the Kenya Amateur Athletics Association (KAAA).
Kiptanui added after the race: "I am now looking forward to defending my title in Athens."
